0.original: Wuk Lamat wishes to seek out the Dawnservant's elector.

48.original: Assuming we have the right idea, one of the Dawnservant's electors should be here somewhere.

49.original: One can tell at a glance how very different the Hanu culture is to the Vanu's.

50.original: The water from the falls must flood the wetlands and flow into all these streams and rivers...

51.original: I agreed to serve as a guide, not a nursemaid.

52.original: It's like our friend said. The people are in no mood for festivities...

53.original: I can only assume they are still recovering from the damage wrought by the storm.

54.original: Indeed... Well, let's do what we came to do and find this elector.

57.original: It's a Hanu greeting. Surely you heard it the last time you were here.

58.original: Well, I was busy enjoying the festival...

59.original: Greetings to the Third Promise and her entourage! I, Zanuhali, welcome you to Ok'hanu.

60.original: As elder of my people, I shall also be fulfilling the duties of elector during the rite of succession.

61.original: So our idea about the electors was correct. We just do as Papa said, and retrace his path from the saga!

62.original: I'm ready! Give me the feat and test my worth!

63.original: All in good time, all in good time. In fact, I came to let you know that we are not quite ready to begin.

64.original: For the moment, please enjoy the hospitality of our village.

65.original: Should we poke around a bit, then? We might pick up some clues about the feat. You know, prepare ourselves.

67.original: What! You think I'm being too cautious!?

68.original: No, no, I'm impressed, is all. You admire and respect your father, who is prone to decisive action, so I expected you to rush in first and ask questions later. Or never.

69.original: I do look up to Papa, but you should know that he has a pragmatic side too. The Head of Reason is the thinker who takes time to consider all the possibilities.

70.original: With the long naps he takes these days, though, the Head of Resolve is less restrained by his wisdom. I can't fault you for thinking that's all there is to him, but there's more to the Dawnservant you've seen thus far.

71.original: I should like to speak with the Head of Reason one day.

72.original: Ah, well...I'm sure you'll catch him awake soon enough.

73.original: To return to the subject at hand, you wish to take a look around Ok'hanu, then? Do some groundwork before the feat begins?

74.original: Something like that. I mean, I could probably pass this test with my eyes closed, but it'll keep us busy while we're waiting!

75.original: Wuk Lamat has the right of it. As Elder Zanuhali is a resident of this village, learning more about it can only improve our chances in the feat.

76.original: Right, then. It helped to do some investigating at Wachunpelo, so let's take a look around here as well!

77.original: Might I suggest a division of forces? For instance, Erenville, Alisaie, and Krile could concentrate on the southern half of the settlement.

78.original: Meanwhile, Wuk Lamat, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>, and myself will handle this northern half.

80.original: This is even worse than I expected...

82.original: You heard about the storm? I've never seen the likes of it before.

83.original: With the supplies and help the Dawnservant sent, we're making progress repairing and rebuilding our homes...

84.original: But while rooves and walls can be patched, there is so much else that was lost for good...

86.original: The gaping hole in the wall and missing portion of the roof are clearly the work of the storm's powerful winds. Repairs appear to be ongoing.

88.original: A lot of houses are still damaged, and the Hanu I've spoken to are not their usual cheery selves. That storm broke more than wood and reeds.

89.original: There must be something I can do to help them...

90.original: I'm going to look around a bit more.

92.original: The dry and shrunken bundles suggest the reeds were harvested some time ago.

93.original: Woven from reeds, this boat-like vessel is reminiscent of a bird. The beak and feathered tail in particular stand out.

94.original: This boat must be woven from the same reeds I've seen gathered into bundles here and there. The plants hold both practical and cultural significance to the Hanu, then...

96.original: (-Krile-)I'm told they're ready to receive us now. Come to the large building in the south of the village!

98.original: We ought to hurry over, too.
